title: Voice cloning attacks against family and finance
body_md:
## A familiar voice can carry an unfamiliar request

Voice cloning can make a caller sound like somebody you know. The FTC warns that a short clip from online material can be enough for a scammer to attempt it. That does not mean every tool works with a fixed number of seconds, or that every convincing impersonation used AI. Caller ID can be spoofed, a real phone can be stolen, and a relative's distress can sound unusual without deception.

The family-emergency script joins a familiar voice to urgency, secrecy and a payment method that is difficult to recover. The caller may introduce a second voice as a lawyer or official. Staying on the same call to question that person is not an independent check. End the call, dial the relative on a number you saved earlier, and contact another close person if there is no answer. If there might be a genuine emergency, contact the relevant local emergency service through its established number. Do not delay care merely to finish a fraud test.

At work, a voice resembling an executive may request a confidential transfer or a change in supplier details. The voice is irrelevant to the normal approval boundary. Use the approved directory, payment-change procedure and second sign-off. A corporate chat account can also be compromised, so ask the exact person and amount through a known channel rather than treating a green online indicator as proof.

A family phrase can be a useful extra prompt if everyone understands it, but it is **not a master key**. It may be overheard, phished, forgotten under stress or repeated by an attacker after one family member reveals it. Do not use a childhood fact that is searchable online as the sole test. If the phrase is missing or correct, still use the independent callback before sending money. Never tell a caller a one-time account code.

If money was already sent, contact the bank or payment provider promptly and ask what recovery is possible; success is not guaranteed. Follow local reporting routes. The strongest habit is to verify the *request* outside the call, whether or not the voice was synthesized.

widget_config.goal: Verify urgent family or finance calls without relying on a familiar voice.
widget_config.today_action: Save the independently verified number of one close person you would contact during a family emergency.
widget_config.scope: General guidance; FTC examples and reporting routes apply to the US, checked 20 October 2026. Use local emergency and workplace procedures.

sources.title: FTC: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money
sources.scope: US consumer advice, September 2023; voice cloning, urgency, independent callback and another relative. The US reporting route is jurisdiction-specific.

sources.title: FBI IC3: Business Email Compromise
sources.scope: US guidance for transfer and account-change requests; secondary-channel verification and urgent bank contact after a suspected transfer. Organisational and national procedures vary.

blocks.title: A distressed nephew asks for secrecy
blocks.situation: A synthetic caller sounds like your nephew and says an intermediary will accept a payment immediately. He begs you not to contact his parents.
blocks.analysis: Secrecy and urgent payment block checking. End the call, use the nephew’s previously saved number, then contact his parents if needed. A second voice introduced by the caller is still inside the same untrusted conversation.

blocks.title: A genuine emergency sounds unlike the person
blocks.situation: Synthetic example: Your sister calls from a borrowed phone after a traffic accident; noise and panic make her voice hard to recognise. She asks you to come to a hospital, not to send money.
blocks.analysis: A different voice is not proof of fraud. Ask for the hospital name, call its published switchboard or local emergency service if necessary, and act on verified welfare information. Avoid demanding a code phrase before offering real help.

blocks.title: Late-night call from a loved one
blocks.setup: Synthetic scenario: a voice like your brother says he needs urgent financial help. The number is unfamiliar.

steps.prompt: He asks you to keep talking while a “lawyer” explains payment.

choices.text: End this call and use a saved contact
choices.consequence: You make room for an independent check.
choices.explanation: The “lawyer” is chosen by the caller and does not verify the caller.

choices.text: Listen to the lawyer as verification
choices.explanation: Two voices on one controlled call are not two sources.

steps.prompt: The saved number does not answer. What next?

choices.text: Contact another relative or a published institution number
choices.explanation: No answer does not mean the caller’s payment story is true.

choices.consequence: The attacker gets money and may ask for more.
choices.explanation: A test payment is still a payment to an unverified recipient.

steps.prompt: The caller knows your family phrase. Do you pay?

choices.text: Wait for independent confirmation of the person and request
choices.consequence: The phrase becomes one clue, not permission to pay.
choices.explanation: A shared phrase can leak or be elicited; verify through a saved route.

choices.text: Pay because only family knows the phrase
choices.consequence: The simulated payment goes to an unverified recipient.
choices.explanation: Knowledge of a phrase is not independent confirmation.

blocks.debrief: Urgency did not remove the duty to check. If a real emergency is plausible, seek help through known institutions while withholding unverified payments. Replay any step to practise.

questions.prompt: A manager’s familiar voice asks to change supplier bank details. Best next step?

choices.text: Use the documented payment-change and callback process
choices.explanation: Financial controls apply regardless of voice quality.

choices.text: Approve because you recognise the voice
choices.explanation: Cloning and ordinary impersonation make voice alone insufficient.

questions.prompt: A caller knows a private childhood detail. Does that settle identity?

choices.text: No; the detail may have leaked or been researched
choices.explanation: A knowledge question is weaker than a route you choose independently.

choices.text: Yes; a clone cannot know facts
choices.explanation: The human attacker can supply facts to a model or speak directly.

questions.prompt: The real person cannot be reached, but danger may be genuine.

choices.text: Contact another trusted person or local emergency service; do not make an unverified payment
choices.explanation: You can check welfare promptly without accepting the caller’s payment channel.

choices.text: Ignore every emergency until the person calls back
choices.explanation: A real emergency may require a prompt call to a reliable institution.
